Hi. These warnings arise due to the fact that `pacman` works in a `fakeroot` environment from an ordinary user, it does not affect anything. If you want, you can run `pacman` with sending stderr to /dev/null (pacman -S ... 2>/dev/null) or you can use `proot -0 /bin/pacman` for run `pacman` in a `fakeroot` environment, but it works more slowly

https://proot-me.github.io
https://salsa.debian.org/clint/fakeroot

Hello @fwn0 , in the [next runimage release](https://github.com/VHSgunzo/runimage/blob/v0.39.1), the systemd package has been replaced by the [fake systemd](https://github.com/VHSgunzo/runimage-fake-systemd), but so that all packages that require it do not resent this. 
It was possible to achieve the operability of services inside the container (python3 required), but some of them still need to be edited.
Also, by default, the systemd of the system (if there is one) will be hidden inside the runimage, but the ability to share systemd is left using the variable `SHARE_SYSTEMD=1`

If you like, I can give you the current [test container](https://huggingface.co/runimage/releases/tree/main/unstable/v0.39.1.23.08.09.121743) of the future runimage release
All changes can be viewed [here](https://github.com/VHSgunzo/runimage/blob/v0.39.1/CHANGELOG.md)

As for the artix bootstrap, I will try to make a test release on it and if there is no problem, perhaps runimage will switch to rootfs from artix.

@VHSgunzo How about this ?

```sh
share_nvidia_driver(){
	# NVIDIA driver integration. This is straight from https://github.com/89luca89/distrobox/blob/main/distrobox-init#L1478,

	# First we find all non-lib files we need, this includes
	#	- binaries
	#	- egl files
	#	- icd files
	#	Excluding here the libs, we will treat them later specifically
	NVIDIA_FILES="$(find /usr/share/vulkan/ /usr/share/egl/ /usr/bin/ \
		-iname "*nvidia*" -not -type d -print 2> /dev/null || :)"
	for nvidia_file in ${NVIDIA_FILES}; do
		NVIDIA_DRIVER_BIND+=("--ro-bind-try"  "${nvidia_file}" "${nvidia_file}")
	done

        # Then we find all directories with nvidia in the name and just mount them
	NVIDIA_DIRS="$(find /usr/lib -iname "*nvidia*" -type d 2> /dev/null || :)"
	for nvidia_dir in ${NVIDIA_DIRS}; do
		if printf "%s" "${nvidia_dir}" | grep -Eq "x86_64-linux-gnu|i386-linux-gnu"; then
			# Remove origin so we plug our own
			dest_dir=$(printf "%s" "${nvidia_dir}" |
				sed "s|/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/|/usr/lib64/|g" |
				sed "s|/usr/lib/i386-linux-gnu/|/usr/lib32/|g")
		else
			dest_dir="${nvidia_dir}"
		fi

		NVIDIA_DRIVER_BIND+=("--ro-bind-try"  "${nvidia_dir}" "${dest_dir}")
	done	
	
	# Then we find all the ".so" libraries, they are searched separately
	# because we need to extract the relative path to mount them in the
	# correct path based on the guest's setup
	#
	# /usr/lib64 is common in Arch or RPM based distros, while /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu is
	# common on Debian derivatives, so we need to adapt between the two nomenclatures.
	NVIDIA_LIBS="$(ldconfig -p | awk '/nvidia/{print $4}' \
	&& ldconfig -p | awk '/libcuda/{print $4}'  \
	&& ldconfig -p | awk '/libnvoptix/{print $4}' \
	&& ldconfig -p | awk '/libnvcuvid/{print $4}' 2> /dev/null || :)"
	for nvidia_lib in ${NVIDIA_LIBS}; do
		if printf "%s" "$nvidia_lib" | grep -Eq "x86_64-linux-gnu|i386-linux-gnu"; then
			# Remove origin so we plug our own
			dest_dir=$(printf "%s" "$nvidia_lib" |
				sed "s|/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/|/usr/lib64/|g" |
				sed "s|/usr/lib/i386-linux-gnu/|/usr/lib32/|g")
		else
			dest_dir="${nvidia_lib}"
		fi

		# If file exists, just continue
		# this may happen for directories like /usr/lib/nvidia/xorg/foo.so
		# where the directory is already bind mounted (ro) and we don't need
		# to mount further files in it.
		if [ -e "$dest_dir" ]; then
			continue
		fi

		type="file"
		if [ -L "${nvidia_lib}" ]; then
			type="link"
		fi

		if [ "${type}" = "link" ]; then
			mkdir -p "$(dirname "${dest_dir}")"
			cp -d "${nvidia_lib}" "${dest_dir}"
			continue
		fi
		NVIDIA_DRIVER_BIND+=("--ro-bind-try"  "${nvidia_lib}" "${dest_dir}")
	done

	# Refresh ldconfig cache, also detect if there are empty files remaining
	# and clean them.
	# This could happen when upgrading drivers and changing versions.
	empty_libs="$(ldconfig 2>&1 | grep -Eo "File.*is empty" | cut -d' ' -f2)"
	if [ -n "${empty_libs}" ]; then
		# shellcheck disable=SC2086
		find ${empty_libs} -delete 2> /dev/null || :
		find /usr/ -empty -iname "*nvidia*" -delete 2> /dev/null || :
	fi
}
```

> Can you tell me how is it possible to create wine32 as a minimal portable runtime, without depending on 32-bit libs on 64-bit running system?

You can use a script like this:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

cd "$(dirname "$(realpath "$BASH_SOURCE")")"

pre_install() {
    # Download runimage
    if [ ! -e runimage ]
        then
            curl -LO https://github.com/VHSgunzo/runimage/releases/download/v0.39.1/runimage
            chmod +x runimage
    fi

    # Update runimage
    ./runimage --rU -zstd 1
}

run_install() {
    set -e

    # Install wine and dependencies
    pac --needed --noconfirm -Sy wine wine-mono wine-gecko lib32-gnutls gst-plugins-base lib32-gst-plugins-base \
        gst-plugins-base-libs lib32-gst-plugins-base-libs gst-plugins-good lib32-gst-plugins-good libpulse lib32-libpulse \
        libxcomposite lib32-libxcomposite libxinerama lib32-libxinerama alsa-lib lib32-alsa-lib lib32-vulkan-icd-loader \
        vulkan-icd-loader vulkan-mesa-layers vulkan-intel vulkan-radeon vulkan-nouveau vulkan-swrast lib32-vulkan-intel \
        lib32-vulkan-radeon lib32-vulkan-nouveau lib32-vulkan-swrast lib32-libpipewire libpipewire pipewire \
        lib32-libpipewire egl-wayland

    # Shrink (optionally)
    (cd /var && \
    curl -LO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VHSgunzo/runimage/refs/heads/main/runshrink && \
    chmod +x runshrink && \
    ./runshrink)

    # Build new runimage with zstd 22 lvl
    runbuild runimage-wine -zstd 22
}
export -f run_install

post_install() {
    # Create symlink (optionally)
    ln -sfr runimage-wine wine
}

##########################
##########################
##########################

pre_install

##########################

OVERFS_MODE=1 NO_NVIDIA_CHECK=1 \
./runimage bash -c run_install

##########################

post_install
```

Or do it manually and step by step. (You may not need all the dependencies for wine in your case)

@fwn0 
Hi! To fully run docker daemon requires elevated privileges (even for rootless mode). But still I managed to run docker daemon in runimage. Here is a rough order of operations: 
### Create docker dir:
```
mkdir docker
```

### Run runimage in overlayfs mode, with sandbox network and with bubblewrap fake root and with bind docker dir:
```
OVERFS_ID=docker KEEP_OVERFS=1 SANDBOX_NET=1 ./runimage --uid 0 --gid 0 --bind "$PWD/docker" /var/lib/docker bash
```

### Install docker: 
```
# update packages:
rim-update

pac --noconfirm -S docker
```

### Run the docker daemon in the runimage network sandbox on 127.0.0.0.1:1337 : 
```
/usr/bin/dockerd -H tcp://127.0.0.1:1337 --seccomp-profile unconfined --rootless --no-new-privileges &>/dev/null &
```

### And now you can run docker: 
```
DOCKER_HOST=tcp://127.0.0.1:1337 docker run --rm -i -v /dev:/dev alpine:latest cat /etc/os-release 
``` 

### But there are some limitations: 
* I have not yet managed to solve the lchown problem when pull some container images (for example debian:latest)
* You can't remove the -v /dev:/dev bind or you will get the /dev/pts error 
* Even with the -v /dev:/dev bind there is no way to alocate a full-fledged pseudo terminal or you will get the /dev/console error.

I may need to analyze the dockerd source code (runc, containerd) and apply some tricks to fix these errors (as I already did for [runimage-openssh](https://github.com/VHSgunzo/runimage-openssh)). I would be glad to have help in this endeavor.

Alternatively, you can use [udocker](https://github.com/indigo-dc/udocker) as an option. This is not a full-fledged replacement for docker, but it's still not bad either.

> But now I have another problem with user/group. I would like to create jellyfin server with client in RunImage, but as you can see, here is a problem.

By default, runimage bind groups and users from the host, to change this, you can use `RIM_UNSHARE_USERS=1` 
and then you can add groups and users in the container, but there's a catch, because it's a container in the unprivileged user namespaces, you won't be able to really change the user or group, so you can
use, for example, `fakeroot` with the fake user's UID inside the container, if the application really needs to change the user or group during operation (like for apt or pacman).
https://salsa.debian.org/clint/fakeroot/-/blob/master/communicate.h?ref_type=heads#L102-L109
```
FAKEROOTEUID=2 fakeroot id -un 
```
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1853250-099d-4600-8585-ddf03c99fb8f)

In the case of systemd units, you can try to remove user and group changes from the unit.

For jellyfin
```
RIM_OVERFS_ID=jellyfin RIM_KEEP_OVERFS=1 ./runimage

pac -Sy jellyfin-server jellyfin-web
sed -i '/^User/d;/^Group/d' /usr/lib/systemd/system/jellyfin.service
mkdir -p /var/lib/jellyfin
systemctl start jellyfin -vvv
```

or you can add the necessary services to autostart
```
systemctl enable jellyfin -vvv
```
and then use init
```
RIM_OVERFS_ID=jellyfin RIM_KEEP_OVERFS=1 ./runimage systemctl init
```

It's not the whole `apparmor` that is affected, just the prohibition on creating `unprivileged userns`, and this practice "out of the box" is mostly only used in `ubuntu 24+ `

`proot` is much slower because it uses `prtace` and many runimage options will simply not work there, including security and isolation options like process isolation, network sandbox and others.

Got it working On Batocera:

Flatpak already worked for me inside Conty, because Conty handles userns/SUID bwrap automatically.

To get the same thing working inside RunImage, all I had to do was run with RUNTIME_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 so it unpacked onto /userdata (a normal suid-enabled ext4).

That let me set chmod u+s /usr/bin/bwrap → Flatpak’s inner sandbox worked just like in Conty.

On Rocknix:

Harder, because RunImage defaults to /var/RunDir, which is mounted nosuid. Even if you chmod u+s, the kernel ignores it, so Flatpak kept dying with /newroot/proc errors.

Fix was telling RunImage to extract onto /storage (TMPDIR=/storage/runimage-tmp), which does honor suid.

Once I did that, suid on bwrap stuck, and Flatpak ran fine. I also added overlay + binds so Flatpak data persists outside.

👉 TL;DR: Batocera worked almost like Conty out of the box. Rocknix needed the extra hoop of moving RunImage’s TMPDIR off a nosuid mount to /storage.

Here's what you would have to do in a normal non-root environment with a regular user to install the flatpak firefox in RunImage:

```
## Download RunImage
ARCH=$(uname -m)
curl -L https://github.com/VHSgunzo/runimage/releases/download/continuous/runimage-$ARCH -o runimage && \
chmod +x runimage

## Run RunImage in OverlayFS mode with ID flatpak and save after closing
################################# RIM_UNSHARE_HOME=1 is optional
RIM_OVERFS_ID=flatpak RIM_KEEP_OVERFS=1 RIM_UNSHARE_HOME=1 ./runimage

## Install flatpak
pac -Sy --noconfirm flatpak

## this alias can also be added to rc files
alias flatpak='flatpak --user'

## Add flathub repo
flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo

## Install firefox
flatpak install org.mozilla.firefox

## Run firefox
flatpak run org.mozilla.firefox
```
